# New submission review

## Has the license been approved by the OSI?
*All OSI-approved license will be included on the SPDX License List, regardless of other factors*

No; I see no evidence that the OSI has approved this exception.

## Definitive factors
*These must all be satisfied to allow inclusion in the license list*

### Is the submitted license unique, that is, it does not match another license already on the License List as per the matching guidelines?

Yes, it is not already on the SPDX License List.

### If a software license, does it apply to source code and not only to executables?

Yes.

### Does the license have identifiable and stable text, and is not in the midst of drafting?

The submitter expressed two distinct exceptions, but both seem to be stable.

### Has the license steward, if any, committed to versioning new versions in the future and to not modify it after addition to the list?

I think we'll ask @hadess to answer this one :smiley:

## Other factors for inclusion
*Roughly in order of descending importance*

### 1. Does the license substantially comply with one of the free/open content definitions?
*Approval by the organisation that publishes the definition is not required*

Yes; it is an exception to the GPL and does not restrict use in any way.

### 2. Is the license structured to be generally usable by anyone, and not specific to one organisation or project?

No, but the language appears to be easily 'templatable'.

### 3. Does the license have substantial use such that it is likely to be encountered (ie. use in many projects, or in one significant project)?
*For recently written licenses, definitive plans for it to be used in at least one or a few significant projects may satisfy this*

Yes, GNOME Videos and Rhythmbox are often pre-installed on major open source desktop distributions, such as Fedora Workstation.

### 4. Is the license primarily intended to facilitate the free distribution of content with limited restrictions?

Yes.

### 5. Does the license steward support this submission, or is at least aware of and not in opposition of it?

Yes, it seems! :grinning:

## Summary of factors / outcome
*Comments on the totality of these "other factors" in light of the SPDX License List's overall goals and objectives*

I am in favour of including this exception in the SPDX License List. It satisfies the license inclusion principles, apart from some technical details which can be resolved with templating and/or upstream coordination.

@hadess, welcome to SPDX! Thank you for making this request; I've left some comments above about the exception's suitability, following our [license inclusion principles](https://github.com/spdx/license-list-XML/blob/master/DOCS/license-inclusion-principles.md). We have our fortnightly SPDX Legal Team meeting next Thursday, which is when we'll probably make a final decision; you're welcome to join if you would like!

Thanks very much for the quick review!

Before setting the license in stone (at least this version), I might want to take some time to reach out to the other users of the exception so we can agree on using the better reworded version from Rhythmbox for all the uses. Would it be helpful for the exception to be made more generic (eg. not including the project name but "this project") before voting on the inclusion?

I'm not going to be available Thursday next week, but I could definitely join on the 28th, and I would be very interested in doing so, if that's feasible on your side. What do you reckon?

Thank you @hadess and thanks @seabass-labrax for the quick analysis!

@hadess yes, if totem is likely to switch to a version that the other projects are also using, that might be helpful to do first. Although the prior distributions of course will have used the prior version of the exception, if you're moving forward with the new one then we'd probably lean towards using that. In particular if it aligns with what the other projects are using, since that contributes to the "substantial use" factor that @seabass-labrax analyzed above.

As far as "templating" goes, we sometimes incorporate markup to reflect "replaceable" text such as project names into the license text XML files if and when they are accepted. So it's up to you and your community whether you use a "this project" generic formulation for the license text, or whether you stick with referencing Totem. 

Personally I tend to prefer the "generic"-style license texts whenever possible, simply because that means less customization and therefore less hassle for everyone when detecting / analyzing and complying with the license. But again, up to you and your community  :)
thanks all - I'm marking this for the next release, but if there are subsequent changes, we may need to push it out
+1 to add.
Discussed on legal team call 2022-04-14, agreed to add each of these, with templating out the Rhythmbox name.

I'm back at work today, and I'm happy to see that the license was accepted.

I would have wanted this text to be used instead of templating the Rhythmbox one if that's still possible:
```
This project hereby grants permission for non-GPL compatible GStreamer plugins
to be used and distributed together with GStreamer and this project. This
permission is above and beyond the permissions granted by the GPL license
by which this project is covered. If you modify this code, you may extend this
exception to your version of the code, but you are not obligated to do so. 
If you do not wish to do so, delete this exception statement from your version.
```

The differences are minor, just replacing "Rhythmbox" by "this project" to avoid the need for templating.

If a project must be using this exact wording, then I can merge this changeset right now:
https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/totem/-/merge_requests/274
I'm available this Wednesday if my presence is needed to discuss the changes I proposed above.

The meetings are Thursdays, and I've added tomorrow's to my calendar. See you then!

@hadess, great to hear that! :grinning:

As for this text:

> This project hereby grants permission for non-GPL compatible GStreamer plugins
> to be used and distributed together with GStreamer and this project. This
> permission is above and beyond the permissions granted by the GPL license
> by which this project is covered. If you modify this code, you may extend this
> exception to your version of the code, but you are not obligated to do so. 
> If you do not wish to do so, delete this exception statement from your version.

That's great! It would reduce the likelihood of new variants being accidentally created if other projects started using this exception, which is a good thing for software composition analysis! It would probably be wise to add templating in the SPDX License List anyway though, as then the entry would match older versions of the exception, for instance copies of GNOME Videos in more stable distributions. If someone was to copy the plain text from SPDX though (which for instance the [REUSE](https://reuse.software) tool does) they would get the new, generic version.

Does that sound good for you too? If so, I think we can get this in for the next SPDX License List release :)

Just looking over the PR for this and wanted to clarify one thing:
- the difference in terms a name (Rhythmbox) v. a generic reference (this project) does not make a need for a different exception entry as this difference is not legally substantive. In which case, we would use the "replaceable" markup to show that whether these is a specific name or generic reference, it is still a match for the license.
- but I see a substantive difference in the presense of this sentensce "If you modify this code, you may extend this
exception to your version of the code, but you are not obligated to do so. 
If you do not wish to do so, delete this exception statement from your version." which does not seem to appear on the "old" version. 

Is that right?  I'm not clear if this was what was discussed or not in terms of the decision to add two exceptions.

> * the difference in terms a name (Rhythmbox) v. a generic reference (this project) does not make a need for a different exception entry as this difference is not legally substantive. In which case, we would use the "replaceable" markup to show that whether these is a specific name or generic reference, it is still a match for the license.

I don't see any `replaceable` markup (I grepped for "replaceable" in the sources, and that code isn't used anywhere). I used:
```
<alt match=".+" name="project">This project</alt>
```
for the replaceable sections, which is what other licenses with replaceable parts seemed to do. If that doesn't match what you expect, can you please point me to a license definition that uses that "replaceable" markup?

> * but I see a substantive difference in the presense of this sentensce "If you modify this code, you may extend this
>   exception to your version of the code, but you are not obligated to do so.
>   If you do not wish to do so, delete this exception statement from your version." which does not seem to appear on the "old" version.

This is a clarification of `This permission are above and beyond the permissions granted by the GPL license Totem is covered by.` which makes the source code in those projects compatible with other GPLv2+ projects without the exception.

now having re-read comments here and in the PR: It looks like the decision on 4/14 legal call was to "add each of these"  - which I assumed to mean the two variants (2005 and 2008) as included in @hadess 's first comment here.

It also seems that templatizing the name in both variants - such that whether it says Totem / this project / Rhythmbox - it will still be a match (as per guideline 2.1.3 https://spdx.dev/license-list/matching-guidelines/ ) was also decided upon.

What seems to be missing, is a discussion or decision on the short identifiers for each, which is key since we endeavor to never change these. The PR has "GPL-GStreamer-exception" and "GPL-GStreamer-exception-old" - which is a bit different than what we usually do for multiple versions, which is to use a version number or a year/date. I also thought we were trying to avoid having "GPL" or other license names in the id for the exception?

I'm sorry I missed this - not sure if this was discussed or not previously? (@swinslow @seabass-labrax - thoughts?)
but I should have caught and raised this on the last call in any case.

I'd think that for short ids, it'd be more appropriate to use:
GStreamer-exception-2005
GStreamer-exception-2008

(in the unlikely event it is changed in the future, by having the year, there is still a way to differentiate future versions as well)
